2. Alex's sentence: "tools are what the connector can do" (QUALIFIED)
QUALIFIED: right for connectors, but not the whole picture.
A connector's tools are the actions it lets the AI take. The MCP spec defines tools as functions that let the model perform actions or retrieve information, and the model decides when to call them.
A connector can also offer data (resources) and ready-made templates (prompts), which are not tools.
Many tools belong to no connector: built-ins such as web search and the shell, Claude's server tools and Composio's meta tools.
The MCP spec itself uses "connector" for the link inside the AI app; vendors, like Alex, use it for the service side.
A tool can be listed and still be blocked by the account's permissions or the app's approval settings.
A tool is one action an AI can call. A connector's tools are what that connector lets the AI do; the AI app also has built-in tools that need no connector.

Four things: OpenAI's 2026 plugin (shared by ChatGPT and Codex), the retired 2023 ChatGPT plugin, the Claude Code plugin, and the Claude app or Cowork plugin (same family as Claude Code's, synced to it). Both vendors use a plugin.json file in different folders.

ChatGPT said "connector" until 2025-12-18, then "app"; since July 2026 apps ship inside plugins, and OpenAI's developer docs still say connector. Anthropic says connector for remote MCP in the Claude app, desktop extension for local MCP in Claude Desktop, and MCP server in Claude Code. The MCP spec uses connector for the link inside the AI app.

MCP: one function a server offers. Composio: one action, plus meta tools. OpenAI API: anything in the tools list (built-ins, your functions, remote MCP). Claude API: client tools you run and server tools Anthropic runs.
One format everywhere (SKILL.md, the open Agent Skills standard); each app reads different folders.
